title: Sworn in as special assistant to the Cumberland County DA
summary: At his Portland concert in December 1978 the district attorney swears Leeman in and gives him a Miranda warning card.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: While being a guest in my home town of Portland, Maine last December -- I covered that in some tapes before, when my union presented me with a plaque, the District Attorney was present while I was setting up the drums, and he said he had heard about my accumulating standing as a peace officer in the different states, and he had heard of my father's standing in the past, and I told him that in all my travels around this country, and sheriff's appointments in other states, that with my family's background, I didn't have anything from home, from Portland -- and in the middle of my concert when the union presented me with the bronze plaque that I mentioned before, the District Attorney, Henry Berry III, intervened in the ceremony and told the audience he had been trying to reach the high sheriff all day, and to have him swear me in as a commissioned Cumberland County, Maine sheriff, but said he couldn't find him, as he was busy on a case, the sheriff, that is.

So he went to his office and brought back a state of Maine, Cumberland County District Attorney Commission, signed and sealed, and swore me in then and there as a duly appointed special assistant to the District Attorney, Cumberland County, Maine, the 16th of December, 1978.
At the same time, he also gave me an embossed Miranda warning, rights to be read to a perpetrator in the case of a crime. At this point in my life, I'm going to

point out that it might be a task for me to put a cadiver under arrest, even at the point of my pearl handled Colt .357 magnum, and another thing - wearing handcuffs would get in the way of my drumming; it would hinder me. I sure deviated just now, but the Jim Fulcher story and the parties also pertains to my life, it's part of it, as it were.
